            <div class="column full">
                <h1>Tutorials</h1>
                
            </div>
        </div>
    </div>

    <section class='page_content'>
        <div class='container'>
            <div class='row clearfix'>
                <div class='column full'>
                    <p>🛈 As everything created by the <span class="caps">GIMP</span> project, these tutorials are fully
community-written. Therefore if you find any tutorial incomplete,
or if it contains errors or outdated information, the best thing is to
contribute a fix. Moreover we warmly welcome new tutorials. <a href="#contributing-new-tutorials-or-fixes">See below
for the full contribution
procedure</a>.🛈</p>
<h2 id="beginner">Beginner<a class="headerlink" href="#beginner" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/GIMP_Quickies/"><span class="caps">GIMP</span> Quickies</a><br>
Use <span class="caps">GIMP</span> for simple graphics needs without having to learn advanced image manipulation&nbsp;methods.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Floating_Logo/">Simple Floating Logo</a><br>
This tutorial walks through some basic image and layer manipulation&nbsp;techniques.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/CircleImage/">Making a Circle-Shaped Image</a><br>
How to create a circular-shaped&nbsp;image.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Heart_Shape/">Making a Heart Shape with Selections</a><br>
How to create a heart-shape with&nbsp;selections.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Layer_Masks/">Layer Masks</a><br>
An introduction to using layer masks to modify the opacity of a&nbsp;layer.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Basic_Color_Curves/">Basic Color Curves</a><br>
A first look at the Curves tool and adjusting color tones in an&nbsp;image.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/GIMPProfile/">Your <span class="caps">GIMP</span> Profile (and You)</a><br>
What the <span class="caps">GIMP</span> Profile is and how to use&nbsp;it.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/ImageFormats/">Image Formats Overview</a><br>
Selecting the best image format for your&nbsp;purposes.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Asset_Folders/">Asset Folders</a><br>
Extending <span class="caps">GIMP</span> with new plug-ins, scripts, brushes, and&nbsp;more.</p>
<h2 id="photo-editing">Photo Editing<a class="headerlink" href="#photo-editing" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Digital_Black_and_White_Conversion/">Digital B&amp;W Conversion</a><br>
Detailed conversion tutorial for generating a B&amp;W result from a color&nbsp;image.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Luminosity_Masks/">Luminosity Masks</a><br>
Using multiple layer masks to isolate specific tones in your image for&nbsp;editing.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Tone_Mapping_Using_GIMP_Levels/">Tone Mapping with &#8216;Colors/Exposure&#8217;</a><br>
Using high bit depth <span class="caps">GIMP</span>&#8217;s &#8216;Colors/Exposure&#8217; operation to add exposure compensation to shadows and midtones while retaining highlight&nbsp;details.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Focus_Group/">Focus Group</a><br>
Layer masking and creative filter&nbsp;applications.</p>
<h2 id="painting">Painting<a class="headerlink" href="#painting" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Parametric_Brush/">Parametric Brushes</a><br>
A look at the advantages and flexibility of using Parametric&nbsp;Brushes.</p>
<h2 id="configuration">Configuration<a class="headerlink" href="#configuration" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p><a href="/unix/howtos/tile_cache.html">How to set the tile cache</a><br>
The tile cache tells <span class="caps">GIMP</span> how much memory it can use before swapping some image
data to disk. Setting the size of the tile cache can be critical for the
performance of your&nbsp;system.</p>
<p><a href="/unix/fonts.html">How to install fonts for use with <span class="caps">GIMP</span></a>  </p>
<p><a href="/unix/howtos/gimp-midi.html">How to use <span class="caps">MIDI</span> devices with <span class="caps">GIMP</span></a><br>
<span class="caps">GNU</span>/Linux only&nbsp;procedure.</p>
<h2 id="programming">Programming<a class="headerlink" href="#programming" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Basic_Perl/">Basic <span class="caps">GIMP</span> Perl</a><br>
Learn how to write simple perl scripts using the gimp-perl module (<span class="caps">GNU</span>/Linux users&nbsp;only).</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Automate_Editing_in_GIMP/">Automate Editing</a><br>
Using <span class="caps">GIMP</span> Python to automate a&nbsp;workflow.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/AutomatedJpgToXcf/">Automatic Creation of <span class="caps">XCF</span> from <span class="caps">JPG</span></a><br>
Import <span class="caps">XCF</span> images a directory at a&nbsp;time.</p>
<h2 id="contributing-new-tutorials-or-fixes">Contributing new tutorials or fixes<a class="headerlink" href="#contributing-new-tutorials-or-fixes" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p>You don&#8217;t have to be a developer to participate to the <span class="caps">GIMP</span> project.
Some team members help with design, community management, bug triaging…
and some help with documentation and&nbsp;tutorials!</p>
<p>The only thing we ask of contributors is to use <em>Libre</em> licenses, which
allow anyone to share, redistribute and modify the tutorials. It enables
others to fix tutorials, even years later, even if the original author
is not around anymore. This is the same rules as for our code, making
<span class="caps">GIMP</span> a Free&nbsp;Software.</p>
<p><span id="recommended-licenses"><strong>Recommended licenses</strong></a>&nbsp;are:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://artlibre.org/licence/lal/en/">Free Art&nbsp;1.3</a></li>
<li>Creative Commons <a href="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/">Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0&nbsp;International</a></li>
<li>Creative Commons <a href="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/">Attribution 4.0&nbsp;International</a></li>
<li><a href="https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/"><span class="caps">CC0</span> 1.0 Universal</a>.</li>
</ul>
<p>So you want to contribute? The process is simple, here is an example for
the hypothetical case where you found an error in an existing tutorial.
In such a case of editing existing text, your change will be automatically
considered to be in the same license as chosen by the first&nbsp;author:</p>
<ol>
<li>All tutorial contents can be found on our <a href="https://gitlab.gnome.org/Infrastructure/gimp-web/-/tree/testing/content/tutorials">website&#8217;s
   repository</a>
   (<em>Gitlab</em>). After clicking this link, feel free to browse to understand the file structure: Each
   tutorial is listed in a separate folder and each folder has a file called <code>index.md</code> which
   contains the text of the tutorial. There are many other files that accompany the
   tutorial inside the folder, such as images, screenshots and
   various&nbsp;assets.</li>
<li>Once you found a tutorial, which you want to edit, click the
   <code>index.md</code> link, and you will see a blue button saying &#8220;Edit&#8221;. Click
   it (obviously you need to have created a login first and be&nbsp;connected).</li>
<li><em>Gitlab</em> will propose you to &#8220;fork&#8221; the project because of missing
   permissions.  Press&nbsp;&#8220;fork&#8221;.</li>
<li>Once this is done, make your changes using the
   <a href="https://daringfireball.net/projects/markdown/syntax">Markdown</a>&nbsp;syntax.</li>
<li>When you are happy with your edits, proceed to the bottom of the edit page, notice the &#8220;Commit message&#8221; field.
   Fill in relevant information explaining what you did. Click &#8220;Commit&nbsp;changes&#8221;.</li>
<li>A &#8220;New merge request&#8221; page will appear. Click &#8220;Create merge&nbsp;request&#8221;.</li>
<li>It&#8217;s done! Now all you have to do is wait for one of the core members
   to review and validate your&nbsp;changes.</li>
</ol>
<p>If you just need to change an image (e.g. because it shows an outdated
version of <span class="caps">GIMP</span>), you may select the image in <em>Gitlab</em> and click the
&#8220;Replace&#8221; button. It will propose you to upload a new version and to
write a &#8220;Commit message&#8221; to explain the change. Please write down the
<a href="#recommended-licenses">desired <em>Libre</em> license</a> for the image in the
commit message. Then hit &#8220;Replace&nbsp;file&#8221;.</p>
<p>For more complicated changes, or if you want to propose new tutorials,
it might be necessary to understand at least the basics of the <em>git</em>
source versionning system we use.
Alternatively, you may simply write your tutorial in a new text file on
your machine (following <em>Markdown</em> syntax), then simply <a href="https://gitlab.gnome.org/Infrastructure/gimp-web/-/issues/new">open a
report</a>
and upload all the files (the text file as well as images and other
resources) in this report. Do not forget to tell us the license you
chose from <a href="#recommended-licenses">the list given above</a>.</p>
<hr>
<p><small>
A list of legacy tutorials can be found here:
<a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/list-all.html">All (Legacy) Tutorials&nbsp;List</a></p>
<p>Bear in mind that this list is being provided for legacy reasons only.
They were originally made for very old hence outdated versions of <span class="caps">GIMP</span>
and most of them do no use Libre licenses allowing editing.
</small></p>
                </div>
            </div>
        </div>
    </section>

<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/AutomatedJpgToXcf/">Automatic Creation of <span class="caps">XCF</span> from <span class="caps">JPG</span></a><br>
Import <span class="caps">XCF</span> images a directory at a&nbsp;time.</p>
<h2 id="contributing-new-tutorials-or-fixes">Contributing new tutorials or fixes<a class="headerlink" href="#contributing-new-tutorials-or-fixes" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p>You don&#8217;t have to be a developer to participate to the <span class="caps">GIMP</span> project.
Some team members help with design, community management, bug triaging…
and some help with documentation and&nbsp;tutorials!</p>
<p>The only thing we ask of contributors is to use <em>Libre</em> licenses, which
allow anyone to share, redistribute and modify the tutorials. It enables
others to fix tutorials, even years later, even if the original author
is not around anymore. This is the same rules as for our code, making
<span class="caps">GIMP</span> a Free&nbsp;Software.</p>
<p><span id="recommended-licenses"><strong>Recommended licenses</strong></a>&nbsp;are:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://artlibre.org/licence/lal/en/">Free Art&nbsp;1.3</a></li>
<li>Creative Commons <a href="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/">Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0&nbsp;International</a></li>
<li>Creative Commons <a href="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/">Attribution 4.0&nbsp;International</a></li>
<li><a href="https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/"><span class="caps">CC0</span> 1.0 Universal</a>.</li>
</ul>
<p>So you want to contribute? The process is simple, here is an example for
the hypothetical case where you found an error in an existing tutorial.
In such a case of editing existing text, your change will be automatically
considered to be in the same license as chosen by the first&nbsp;author:</p>
<ol>
<li>All tutorial contents can be found on our <a href="https://gitlab.gnome.org/Infrastructure/gimp-web/-/tree/testing/content/tutorials">website&#8217;s
   repository</a>
   (<em>Gitlab</em>). After clicking this link, feel free to browse to understand the file structure: Each
   tutorial is listed in a separate folder and each folder has a file called <code>index.md</code> which
   contains the text of the tutorial. There are many other files that accompany the
   tutorial inside the folder, such as images, screenshots and
   various&nbsp;assets.</li>
<li>Once you found a tutorial, which you want to edit, click the
   <code>index.md</code> link, and you will see a blue button saying &#8220;Edit&#8221;. Click
   it (obviously you need to have created a login first and be&nbsp;connected).</li>
<li><em>Gitlab</em> will propose you to &#8220;fork&#8221; the project because of missing
   permissions.  Press&nbsp;&#8220;fork&#8221;.</li>
<li>Once this is done, make your changes using the
   <a href="https://daringfireball.net/projects/markdown/syntax">Markdown</a>&nbsp;syntax.</li>
<li>When you are happy with your edits, proceed to the bottom of the edit page, notice the &#8220;Commit message&#8221; field.
   Fill in relevant information explaining what you did. Click &#8220;Commit&nbsp;changes&#8221;.</li>
<li>A &#8220;New merge request&#8221; page will appear. Click &#8220;Create merge&nbsp;request&#8221;.</li>
<li>It&#8217;s done! Now all you have to do is wait for one of the core members
   to review and validate your&nbsp;changes.</li>
</ol>
<p>If you just need to change an image (e.g. because it shows an outdated
version of <span class="caps">GIMP</span>), you may select the image in <em>Gitlab</em> and click the
&#8220;Replace&#8221; button. It will propose you to upload a new version and to
write a &#8220;Commit message&#8221; to explain the change. Please write down the
<a href="#recommended-licenses">desired <em>Libre</em> license</a> for the image in the
commit message. Then hit &#8220;Replace&nbsp;file&#8221;.</p>
<p>For more complicated changes, or if you want to propose new tutorials,
it might be necessary to understand at least the basics of the <em>git</em>
source versionning system we use.
Alternatively, you may simply write your tutorial in a new text file on
your machine (following <em>Markdown</em> syntax), then simply <a href="https://gitlab.gnome.org/Infrastructure/gimp-web/-/issues/new">open a
report</a>
and upload all the files (the text file as well as images and other
resources) in this report. Do not forget to tell us the license you
chose from <a href="#recommended-licenses">the list given above</a>.</p>
<hr>
<p><small>
A list of legacy tutorials can be found here:
<a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/list-all.html">All (Legacy) Tutorials&nbsp;List</a></p>
<p>Bear in mind that this list is being provided for legacy reasons only.
They were originally made for very old hence outdated versions of <span class="caps">GIMP</span>
and most of them do no use Libre licenses allowing editing.
</small></p>
                </div>
            </div>
        </div>
    </section>

            <div class="column full">
                <h1>Tutorials</h1>
                
            </div>
        </div>
    </div>

    <section class='page_content'>
        <div class='container'>
            <div class='row clearfix'>
                <div class='column full'>
                    <p>🛈 As everything created by the <span class="caps">GIMP</span> project, these tutorials are fully
community-written. Therefore if you find any tutorial incomplete,
or if it contains errors or outdated information, the best thing is to
contribute a fix. Moreover we warmly welcome new tutorials. <a href="#contributing-new-tutorials-or-fixes">See below
for the full contribution
procedure</a>.🛈</p>
<h2 id="beginner">Beginner<a class="headerlink" href="#beginner" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/GIMP_Quickies/"><span class="caps">GIMP</span> Quickies</a><br>
Use <span class="caps">GIMP</span> for simple graphics needs without having to learn advanced image manipulation&nbsp;methods.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Floating_Logo/">Simple Floating Logo</a><br>
This tutorial walks through some basic image and layer manipulation&nbsp;techniques.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/CircleImage/">Making a Circle-Shaped Image</a><br>
How to create a circular-shaped&nbsp;image.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Heart_Shape/">Making a Heart Shape with Selections</a><br>
How to create a heart-shape with&nbsp;selections.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Layer_Masks/">Layer Masks</a><br>
An introduction to using layer masks to modify the opacity of a&nbsp;layer.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Basic_Color_Curves/">Basic Color Curves</a><br>
A first look at the Curves tool and adjusting color tones in an&nbsp;image.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/GIMPProfile/">Your <span class="caps">GIMP</span> Profile (and You)</a><br>
What the <span class="caps">GIMP</span> Profile is and how to use&nbsp;it.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/ImageFormats/">Image Formats Overview</a><br>
Selecting the best image format for your&nbsp;purposes.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Asset_Folders/">Asset Folders</a><br>
Extending <span class="caps">GIMP</span> with new plug-ins, scripts, brushes, and&nbsp;more.</p>
<h2 id="photo-editing">Photo Editing<a class="headerlink" href="#photo-editing" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Digital_Black_and_White_Conversion/">Digital B&amp;W Conversion</a><br>
Detailed conversion tutorial for generating a B&amp;W result from a color&nbsp;image.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Luminosity_Masks/">Luminosity Masks</a><br>
Using multiple layer masks to isolate specific tones in your image for&nbsp;editing.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Tone_Mapping_Using_GIMP_Levels/">Tone Mapping with &#8216;Colors/Exposure&#8217;</a><br>
Using high bit depth <span class="caps">GIMP</span>&#8217;s &#8216;Colors/Exposure&#8217; operation to add exposure compensation to shadows and midtones while retaining highlight&nbsp;details.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Focus_Group/">Focus Group</a><br>
Layer masking and creative filter&nbsp;applications.</p>
<h2 id="painting">Painting<a class="headerlink" href="#painting" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Parametric_Brush/">Parametric Brushes</a><br>
A look at the advantages and flexibility of using Parametric&nbsp;Brushes.</p>
<h2 id="configuration">Configuration<a class="headerlink" href="#configuration" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p><a href="/unix/howtos/tile_cache.html">How to set the tile cache</a><br>
The tile cache tells <span class="caps">GIMP</span> how much memory it can use before swapping some image
data to disk. Setting the size of the tile cache can be critical for the
performance of your&nbsp;system.</p>
<p><a href="/unix/fonts.html">How to install fonts for use with <span class="caps">GIMP</span></a>  </p>
<p><a href="/unix/howtos/gimp-midi.html">How to use <span class="caps">MIDI</span> devices with <span class="caps">GIMP</span></a><br>
<span class="caps">GNU</span>/Linux only&nbsp;procedure.</p>
<h2 id="programming">Programming<a class="headerlink" href="#programming" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Basic_Perl/">Basic <span class="caps">GIMP</span> Perl</a><br>
Learn how to write simple perl scripts using the gimp-perl module (<span class="caps">GNU</span>/Linux users&nbsp;only).</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Automate_Editing_in_GIMP/">Automate Editing</a><br>
Using <span class="caps">GIMP</span> Python to automate a&nbsp;workflow.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/AutomatedJpgToXcf/">Automatic Creation of <span class="caps">XCF</span> from <span class="caps">JPG</span></a><br>
Import <span class="caps">XCF</span> images a directory at a&nbsp;time.</p>
<h2 id="contributing-new-tutorials-or-fixes">Contributing new tutorials or fixes<a class="headerlink" href="#contributing-new-tutorials-or-fixes" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p>You don&#8217;t have to be a developer to participate to the <span class="caps">GIMP</span> project.
Some team members help with design, community management, bug triaging…
and some help with documentation and&nbsp;tutorials!</p>
<p>The only thing we ask of contributors is to use <em>Libre</em> licenses, which
allow anyone to share, redistribute and modify the tutorials. It enables
others to fix tutorials, even years later, even if the original author
is not around anymore. This is the same rules as for our code, making
<span class="caps">GIMP</span> a Free&nbsp;Software.</p>
<p><span id="recommended-licenses"><strong>Recommended licenses</strong></a>&nbsp;are:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://artlibre.org/licence/lal/en/">Free Art&nbsp;1.3</a></li>
<li>Creative Commons <a href="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/">Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0&nbsp;International</a></li>
<li>Creative Commons <a href="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/">Attribution 4.0&nbsp;International</a></li>
<li><a href="https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/"><span class="caps">CC0</span> 1.0 Universal</a>.</li>
</ul>
<p>So you want to contribute? The process is simple, here is an example for
the hypothetical case where you found an error in an existing tutorial.
In such a case of editing existing text, your change will be automatically
considered to be in the same license as chosen by the first&nbsp;author:</p>
<ol>
<li>All tutorial contents can be found on our <a href="https://gitlab.gnome.org/Infrastructure/gimp-web/-/tree/testing/content/tutorials">website&#8217;s
   repository</a>
   (<em>Gitlab</em>). After clicking this link, feel free to browse to understand the file structure: Each
   tutorial is listed in a separate folder and each folder has a file called <code>index.md</code> which
   contains the text of the tutorial. There are many other files that accompany the
   tutorial inside the folder, such as images, screenshots and
   various&nbsp;assets.</li>
<li>Once you found a tutorial, which you want to edit, click the
   <code>index.md</code> link, and you will see a blue button saying &#8220;Edit&#8221;. Click
   it (obviously you need to have created a login first and be&nbsp;connected).</li>
<li><em>Gitlab</em> will propose you to &#8220;fork&#8221; the project because of missing
   permissions.  Press&nbsp;&#8220;fork&#8221;.</li>
<li>Once this is done, make your changes using the
   <a href="https://daringfireball.net/projects/markdown/syntax">Markdown</a>&nbsp;syntax.</li>
<li>When you are happy with your edits, proceed to the bottom of the edit page, notice the &#8220;Commit message&#8221; field.
   Fill in relevant information explaining what you did. Click &#8220;Commit&nbsp;changes&#8221;.</li>
<li>A &#8220;New merge request&#8221; page will appear. Click &#8220;Create merge&nbsp;request&#8221;.</li>
<li>It&#8217;s done! Now all you have to do is wait for one of the core members
   to review and validate your&nbsp;changes.</li>
</ol>
<p>If you just need to change an image (e.g. because it shows an outdated
version of <span class="caps">GIMP</span>), you may select the image in <em>Gitlab</em> and click the
&#8220;Replace&#8221; button. It will propose you to upload a new version and to
write a &#8220;Commit message&#8221; to explain the change. Please write down the
<a href="#recommended-licenses">desired <em>Libre</em> license</a> for the image in the
commit message. Then hit &#8220;Replace&nbsp;file&#8221;.</p>
<p>For more complicated changes, or if you want to propose new tutorials,
it might be necessary to understand at least the basics of the <em>git</em>
source versionning system we use.
Alternatively, you may simply write your tutorial in a new text file on
your machine (following <em>Markdown</em> syntax), then simply <a href="https://gitlab.gnome.org/Infrastructure/gimp-web/-/issues/new">open a
report</a>
and upload all the files (the text file as well as images and other
resources) in this report. Do not forget to tell us the license you
chose from <a href="#recommended-licenses">the list given above</a>.</p>
<hr>
<p><small>
A list of legacy tutorials can be found here:
<a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/list-all.html">All (Legacy) Tutorials&nbsp;List</a></p>
<p>Bear in mind that this list is being provided for legacy reasons only.
They were originally made for very old hence outdated versions of <span class="caps">GIMP</span>
and most of them do no use Libre licenses allowing editing.
</small></p>
                </div>
            </div>
        </div>
    </section>

        <div class="row clearfix">
            <div class="column full">
                <h1>Tutorials</h1>
                
            </div>
        </div>
    </div>

    <section class='page_content'>
        <div class='container'>
            <div class='row clearfix'>
                <div class='column full'>
                    <p>🛈 As everything created by the <span class="caps">GIMP</span> project, these tutorials are fully
community-written. Therefore if you find any tutorial incomplete,
or if it contains errors or outdated information, the best thing is to
contribute a fix. Moreover we warmly welcome new tutorials. <a href="#contributing-new-tutorials-or-fixes">See below
for the full contribution
procedure</a>.🛈</p>
<h2 id="beginner">Beginner<a class="headerlink" href="#beginner" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/GIMP_Quickies/"><span class="caps">GIMP</span> Quickies</a><br>
Use <span class="caps">GIMP</span> for simple graphics needs without having to learn advanced image manipulation&nbsp;methods.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Floating_Logo/">Simple Floating Logo</a><br>
This tutorial walks through some basic image and layer manipulation&nbsp;techniques.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/CircleImage/">Making a Circle-Shaped Image</a><br>
How to create a circular-shaped&nbsp;image.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Heart_Shape/">Making a Heart Shape with Selections</a><br>
How to create a heart-shape with&nbsp;selections.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Layer_Masks/">Layer Masks</a><br>
An introduction to using layer masks to modify the opacity of a&nbsp;layer.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Basic_Color_Curves/">Basic Color Curves</a><br>
A first look at the Curves tool and adjusting color tones in an&nbsp;image.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/GIMPProfile/">Your <span class="caps">GIMP</span> Profile (and You)</a><br>
What the <span class="caps">GIMP</span> Profile is and how to use&nbsp;it.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/ImageFormats/">Image Formats Overview</a><br>
Selecting the best image format for your&nbsp;purposes.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Asset_Folders/">Asset Folders</a><br>
Extending <span class="caps">GIMP</span> with new plug-ins, scripts, brushes, and&nbsp;more.</p>
<h2 id="photo-editing">Photo Editing<a class="headerlink" href="#photo-editing" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Digital_Black_and_White_Conversion/">Digital B&amp;W Conversion</a><br>
Detailed conversion tutorial for generating a B&amp;W result from a color&nbsp;image.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Luminosity_Masks/">Luminosity Masks</a><br>
Using multiple layer masks to isolate specific tones in your image for&nbsp;editing.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Tone_Mapping_Using_GIMP_Levels/">Tone Mapping with &#8216;Colors/Exposure&#8217;</a><br>
Using high bit depth <span class="caps">GIMP</span>&#8217;s &#8216;Colors/Exposure&#8217; operation to add exposure compensation to shadows and midtones while retaining highlight&nbsp;details.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Focus_Group/">Focus Group</a><br>
Layer masking and creative filter&nbsp;applications.</p>
<h2 id="painting">Painting<a class="headerlink" href="#painting" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Parametric_Brush/">Parametric Brushes</a><br>
A look at the advantages and flexibility of using Parametric&nbsp;Brushes.</p>
<h2 id="configuration">Configuration<a class="headerlink" href="#configuration" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p><a href="/unix/howtos/tile_cache.html">How to set the tile cache</a><br>
The tile cache tells <span class="caps">GIMP</span> how much memory it can use before swapping some image
data to disk. Setting the size of the tile cache can be critical for the
performance of your&nbsp;system.</p>
<p><a href="/unix/fonts.html">How to install fonts for use with <span class="caps">GIMP</span></a>  </p>
<p><a href="/unix/howtos/gimp-midi.html">How to use <span class="caps">MIDI</span> devices with <span class="caps">GIMP</span></a><br>
<span class="caps">GNU</span>/Linux only&nbsp;procedure.</p>
<h2 id="programming">Programming<a class="headerlink" href="#programming" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Basic_Perl/">Basic <span class="caps">GIMP</span> Perl</a><br>
Learn how to write simple perl scripts using the gimp-perl module (<span class="caps">GNU</span>/Linux users&nbsp;only).</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Automate_Editing_in_GIMP/">Automate Editing</a><br>
Using <span class="caps">GIMP</span> Python to automate a&nbsp;workflow.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/AutomatedJpgToXcf/">Automatic Creation of <span class="caps">XCF</span> from <span class="caps">JPG</span></a><br>
Import <span class="caps">XCF</span> images a directory at a&nbsp;time.</p>
<h2 id="contributing-new-tutorials-or-fixes">Contributing new tutorials or fixes<a class="headerlink" href="#contributing-new-tutorials-or-fixes" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p>You don&#8217;t have to be a developer to participate to the <span class="caps">GIMP</span> project.
Some team members help with design, community management, bug triaging…
and some help with documentation and&nbsp;tutorials!</p>
<p>The only thing we ask of contributors is to use <em>Libre</em> licenses, which
allow anyone to share, redistribute and modify the tutorials. It enables
others to fix tutorials, even years later, even if the original author
is not around anymore. This is the same rules as for our code, making
<span class="caps">GIMP</span> a Free&nbsp;Software.</p>
<p><span id="recommended-licenses"><strong>Recommended licenses</strong></a>&nbsp;are:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://artlibre.org/licence/lal/en/">Free Art&nbsp;1.3</a></li>
<li>Creative Commons <a href="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/">Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0&nbsp;International</a></li>
<li>Creative Commons <a href="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/">Attribution 4.0&nbsp;International</a></li>
<li><a href="https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/"><span class="caps">CC0</span> 1.0 Universal</a>.</li>
</ul>
<p>So you want to contribute? The process is simple, here is an example for
the hypothetical case where you found an error in an existing tutorial.
In such a case of editing existing text, your change will be automatically
considered to be in the same license as chosen by the first&nbsp;author:</p>
<ol>
<li>All tutorial contents can be found on our <a href="https://gitlab.gnome.org/Infrastructure/gimp-web/-/tree/testing/content/tutorials">website&#8217;s
   repository</a>
   (<em>Gitlab</em>). After clicking this link, feel free to browse to understand the file structure: Each
   tutorial is listed in a separate folder and each folder has a file called <code>index.md</code> which
   contains the text of the tutorial. There are many other files that accompany the
   tutorial inside the folder, such as images, screenshots and
   various&nbsp;assets.</li>
<li>Once you found a tutorial, which you want to edit, click the
   <code>index.md</code> link, and you will see a blue button saying &#8220;Edit&#8221;. Click
   it (obviously you need to have created a login first and be&nbsp;connected).</li>
<li><em>Gitlab</em> will propose you to &#8220;fork&#8221; the project because of missing
   permissions.  Press&nbsp;&#8220;fork&#8221;.</li>
<li>Once this is done, make your changes using the
   <a href="https://daringfireball.net/projects/markdown/syntax">Markdown</a>&nbsp;syntax.</li>
<li>When you are happy with your edits, proceed to the bottom of the edit page, notice the &#8220;Commit message&#8221; field.
   Fill in relevant information explaining what you did. Click &#8220;Commit&nbsp;changes&#8221;.</li>
<li>A &#8220;New merge request&#8221; page will appear. Click &#8220;Create merge&nbsp;request&#8221;.</li>
<li>It&#8217;s done! Now all you have to do is wait for one of the core members
   to review and validate your&nbsp;changes.</li>
</ol>
<p>If you just need to change an image (e.g. because it shows an outdated
version of <span class="caps">GIMP</span>), you may select the image in <em>Gitlab</em> and click the
&#8220;Replace&#8221; button. It will propose you to upload a new version and to
write a &#8220;Commit message&#8221; to explain the change. Please write down the
<a href="#recommended-licenses">desired <em>Libre</em> license</a> for the image in the
commit message. Then hit &#8220;Replace&nbsp;file&#8221;.</p>
<p>For more complicated changes, or if you want to propose new tutorials,
it might be necessary to understand at least the basics of the <em>git</em>
source versionning system we use.
Alternatively, you may simply write your tutorial in a new text file on
your machine (following <em>Markdown</em> syntax), then simply <a href="https://gitlab.gnome.org/Infrastructure/gimp-web/-/issues/new">open a
report</a>
and upload all the files (the text file as well as images and other
resources) in this report. Do not forget to tell us the license you
chose from <a href="#recommended-licenses">the list given above</a>.</p>
<hr>
<p><small>
A list of legacy tutorials can be found here:
<a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/list-all.html">All (Legacy) Tutorials&nbsp;List</a></p>
<p>Bear in mind that this list is being provided for legacy reasons only.
They were originally made for very old hence outdated versions of <span class="caps">GIMP</span>
and most of them do no use Libre licenses allowing editing.
</small></p>
                </div>
            </div>
        </div>
    </section>

<p><a href="/unix/fonts.html">How to install fonts for use with <span class="caps">GIMP</span></a>  </p>
<p><a href="/unix/howtos/gimp-midi.html">How to use <span class="caps">MIDI</span> devices with <span class="caps">GIMP</span></a><br>
<span class="caps">GNU</span>/Linux only&nbsp;procedure.</p>
<h2 id="programming">Programming<a class="headerlink" href="#programming" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Basic_Perl/">Basic <span class="caps">GIMP</span> Perl</a><br>
Learn how to write simple perl scripts using the gimp-perl module (<span class="caps">GNU</span>/Linux users&nbsp;only).</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Automate_Editing_in_GIMP/">Automate Editing</a><br>
Using <span class="caps">GIMP</span> Python to automate a&nbsp;workflow.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/AutomatedJpgToXcf/">Automatic Creation of <span class="caps">XCF</span> from <span class="caps">JPG</span></a><br>
Import <span class="caps">XCF</span> images a directory at a&nbsp;time.</p>
<h2 id="contributing-new-tutorials-or-fixes">Contributing new tutorials or fixes<a class="headerlink" href="#contributing-new-tutorials-or-fixes" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p>You don&#8217;t have to be a developer to participate to the <span class="caps">GIMP</span> project.
Some team members help with design, community management, bug triaging…
and some help with documentation and&nbsp;tutorials!</p>
<p>The only thing we ask of contributors is to use <em>Libre</em> licenses, which
allow anyone to share, redistribute and modify the tutorials. It enables
others to fix tutorials, even years later, even if the original author
is not around anymore. This is the same rules as for our code, making
<span class="caps">GIMP</span> a Free&nbsp;Software.</p>
<p><span id="recommended-licenses"><strong>Recommended licenses</strong></a>&nbsp;are:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://artlibre.org/licence/lal/en/">Free Art&nbsp;1.3</a></li>
<li>Creative Commons <a href="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/">Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0&nbsp;International</a></li>
<li>Creative Commons <a href="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/">Attribution 4.0&nbsp;International</a></li>
<li><a href="https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/"><span class="caps">CC0</span> 1.0 Universal</a>.</li>
</ul>
<p>So you want to contribute? The process is simple, here is an example for
the hypothetical case where you found an error in an existing tutorial.
In such a case of editing existing text, your change will be automatically
considered to be in the same license as chosen by the first&nbsp;author:</p>
<ol>
<li>All tutorial contents can be found on our <a href="https://gitlab.gnome.org/Infrastructure/gimp-web/-/tree/testing/content/tutorials">website&#8217;s
   repository</a>
   (<em>Gitlab</em>). After clicking this link, feel free to browse to understand the file structure: Each
   tutorial is listed in a separate folder and each folder has a file called <code>index.md</code> which
   contains the text of the tutorial. There are many other files that accompany the
   tutorial inside the folder, such as images, screenshots and
   various&nbsp;assets.</li>
<li>Once you found a tutorial, which you want to edit, click the
   <code>index.md</code> link, and you will see a blue button saying &#8220;Edit&#8221;. Click
   it (obviously you need to have created a login first and be&nbsp;connected).</li>
<li><em>Gitlab</em> will propose you to &#8220;fork&#8221; the project because of missing
   permissions.  Press&nbsp;&#8220;fork&#8221;.</li>
<li>Once this is done, make your changes using the
   <a href="https://daringfireball.net/projects/markdown/syntax">Markdown</a>&nbsp;syntax.</li>
<li>When you are happy with your edits, proceed to the bottom of the edit page, notice the &#8220;Commit message&#8221; field.
   Fill in relevant information explaining what you did. Click &#8220;Commit&nbsp;changes&#8221;.</li>
<li>A &#8220;New merge request&#8221; page will appear. Click &#8220;Create merge&nbsp;request&#8221;.</li>
<li>It&#8217;s done! Now all you have to do is wait for one of the core members
   to review and validate your&nbsp;changes.</li>
</ol>
<p>If you just need to change an image (e.g. because it shows an outdated
version of <span class="caps">GIMP</span>), you may select the image in <em>Gitlab</em> and click the
&#8220;Replace&#8221; button. It will propose you to upload a new version and to
write a &#8220;Commit message&#8221; to explain the change. Please write down the
<a href="#recommended-licenses">desired <em>Libre</em> license</a> for the image in the
commit message. Then hit &#8220;Replace&nbsp;file&#8221;.</p>
<p>For more complicated changes, or if you want to propose new tutorials,
it might be necessary to understand at least the basics of the <em>git</em>
source versionning system we use.
Alternatively, you may simply write your tutorial in a new text file on
your machine (following <em>Markdown</em> syntax), then simply <a href="https://gitlab.gnome.org/Infrastructure/gimp-web/-/issues/new">open a
report</a>
and upload all the files (the text file as well as images and other
resources) in this report. Do not forget to tell us the license you
chose from <a href="#recommended-licenses">the list given above</a>.</p>
<hr>
<p><small>
A list of legacy tutorials can be found here:
<a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/list-all.html">All (Legacy) Tutorials&nbsp;List</a></p>
<p>Bear in mind that this list is being provided for legacy reasons only.
They were originally made for very old hence outdated versions of <span class="caps">GIMP</span>
and most of them do no use Libre licenses allowing editing.
</small></p>
                </div>
            </div>
        </div>
    </section>

            <div class="column full">
                <h1>Tutorials</h1>
                
            </div>
        </div>
    </div>

    <section class='page_content'>
        <div class='container'>
            <div class='row clearfix'>
                <div class='column full'>
                    <p>🛈 As everything created by the <span class="caps">GIMP</span> project, these tutorials are fully
community-written. Therefore if you find any tutorial incomplete,
or if it contains errors or outdated information, the best thing is to
contribute a fix. Moreover we warmly welcome new tutorials. <a href="#contributing-new-tutorials-or-fixes">See below
for the full contribution
procedure</a>.🛈</p>
<h2 id="beginner">Beginner<a class="headerlink" href="#beginner" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/GIMP_Quickies/"><span class="caps">GIMP</span> Quickies</a><br>
Use <span class="caps">GIMP</span> for simple graphics needs without having to learn advanced image manipulation&nbsp;methods.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Floating_Logo/">Simple Floating Logo</a><br>
This tutorial walks through some basic image and layer manipulation&nbsp;techniques.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/CircleImage/">Making a Circle-Shaped Image</a><br>
How to create a circular-shaped&nbsp;image.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Heart_Shape/">Making a Heart Shape with Selections</a><br>
How to create a heart-shape with&nbsp;selections.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Layer_Masks/">Layer Masks</a><br>
An introduction to using layer masks to modify the opacity of a&nbsp;layer.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Basic_Color_Curves/">Basic Color Curves</a><br>
A first look at the Curves tool and adjusting color tones in an&nbsp;image.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/GIMPProfile/">Your <span class="caps">GIMP</span> Profile (and You)</a><br>
What the <span class="caps">GIMP</span> Profile is and how to use&nbsp;it.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/ImageFormats/">Image Formats Overview</a><br>
Selecting the best image format for your&nbsp;purposes.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Asset_Folders/">Asset Folders</a><br>
Extending <span class="caps">GIMP</span> with new plug-ins, scripts, brushes, and&nbsp;more.</p>
<h2 id="photo-editing">Photo Editing<a class="headerlink" href="#photo-editing" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Digital_Black_and_White_Conversion/">Digital B&amp;W Conversion</a><br>
Detailed conversion tutorial for generating a B&amp;W result from a color&nbsp;image.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Luminosity_Masks/">Luminosity Masks</a><br>
Using multiple layer masks to isolate specific tones in your image for&nbsp;editing.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Tone_Mapping_Using_GIMP_Levels/">Tone Mapping with &#8216;Colors/Exposure&#8217;</a><br>
Using high bit depth <span class="caps">GIMP</span>&#8217;s &#8216;Colors/Exposure&#8217; operation to add exposure compensation to shadows and midtones while retaining highlight&nbsp;details.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Focus_Group/">Focus Group</a><br>
Layer masking and creative filter&nbsp;applications.</p>
<h2 id="painting">Painting<a class="headerlink" href="#painting" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Parametric_Brush/">Parametric Brushes</a><br>
A look at the advantages and flexibility of using Parametric&nbsp;Brushes.</p>
<h2 id="configuration">Configuration<a class="headerlink" href="#configuration" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p><a href="/unix/howtos/tile_cache.html">How to set the tile cache</a><br>
The tile cache tells <span class="caps">GIMP</span> how much memory it can use before swapping some image
data to disk. Setting the size of the tile cache can be critical for the
performance of your&nbsp;system.</p>
<p><a href="/unix/fonts.html">How to install fonts for use with <span class="caps">GIMP</span></a>  </p>
<p><a href="/unix/howtos/gimp-midi.html">How to use <span class="caps">MIDI</span> devices with <span class="caps">GIMP</span></a><br>
<span class="caps">GNU</span>/Linux only&nbsp;procedure.</p>
<h2 id="programming">Programming<a class="headerlink" href="#programming" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Basic_Perl/">Basic <span class="caps">GIMP</span> Perl</a><br>
Learn how to write simple perl scripts using the gimp-perl module (<span class="caps">GNU</span>/Linux users&nbsp;only).</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Automate_Editing_in_GIMP/">Automate Editing</a><br>
Using <span class="caps">GIMP</span> Python to automate a&nbsp;workflow.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/AutomatedJpgToXcf/">Automatic Creation of <span class="caps">XCF</span> from <span class="caps">JPG</span></a><br>
Import <span class="caps">XCF</span> images a directory at a&nbsp;time.</p>
<h2 id="contributing-new-tutorials-or-fixes">Contributing new tutorials or fixes<a class="headerlink" href="#contributing-new-tutorials-or-fixes" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p>You don&#8217;t have to be a developer to participate to the <span class="caps">GIMP</span> project.
Some team members help with design, community management, bug triaging…
and some help with documentation and&nbsp;tutorials!</p>
<p>The only thing we ask of contributors is to use <em>Libre</em> licenses, which
allow anyone to share, redistribute and modify the tutorials. It enables
others to fix tutorials, even years later, even if the original author
is not around anymore. This is the same rules as for our code, making
<span class="caps">GIMP</span> a Free&nbsp;Software.</p>
<p><span id="recommended-licenses"><strong>Recommended licenses</strong></a>&nbsp;are:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://artlibre.org/licence/lal/en/">Free Art&nbsp;1.3</a></li>
<li>Creative Commons <a href="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/">Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0&nbsp;International</a></li>
<li>Creative Commons <a href="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/">Attribution 4.0&nbsp;International</a></li>
<li><a href="https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/"><span class="caps">CC0</span> 1.0 Universal</a>.</li>
</ul>
<p>So you want to contribute? The process is simple, here is an example for
the hypothetical case where you found an error in an existing tutorial.
In such a case of editing existing text, your change will be automatically
considered to be in the same license as chosen by the first&nbsp;author:</p>
<ol>
<li>All tutorial contents can be found on our <a href="https://gitlab.gnome.org/Infrastructure/gimp-web/-/tree/testing/content/tutorials">website&#8217;s
   repository</a>
   (<em>Gitlab</em>). After clicking this link, feel free to browse to understand the file structure: Each
   tutorial is listed in a separate folder and each folder has a file called <code>index.md</code> which
   contains the text of the tutorial. There are many other files that accompany the
   tutorial inside the folder, such as images, screenshots and
   various&nbsp;assets.</li>
<li>Once you found a tutorial, which you want to edit, click the
   <code>index.md</code> link, and you will see a blue button saying &#8220;Edit&#8221;. Click
   it (obviously you need to have created a login first and be&nbsp;connected).</li>
<li><em>Gitlab</em> will propose you to &#8220;fork&#8221; the project because of missing
   permissions.  Press&nbsp;&#8220;fork&#8221;.</li>
<li>Once this is done, make your changes using the
   <a href="https://daringfireball.net/projects/markdown/syntax">Markdown</a>&nbsp;syntax.</li>
<li>When you are happy with your edits, proceed to the bottom of the edit page, notice the &#8220;Commit message&#8221; field.
   Fill in relevant information explaining what you did. Click &#8220;Commit&nbsp;changes&#8221;.</li>
<li>A &#8220;New merge request&#8221; page will appear. Click &#8220;Create merge&nbsp;request&#8221;.</li>
<li>It&#8217;s done! Now all you have to do is wait for one of the core members
   to review and validate your&nbsp;changes.</li>
</ol>
<p>If you just need to change an image (e.g. because it shows an outdated
version of <span class="caps">GIMP</span>), you may select the image in <em>Gitlab</em> and click the
&#8220;Replace&#8221; button. It will propose you to upload a new version and to
write a &#8220;Commit message&#8221; to explain the change. Please write down the
<a href="#recommended-licenses">desired <em>Libre</em> license</a> for the image in the
commit message. Then hit &#8220;Replace&nbsp;file&#8221;.</p>
<p>For more complicated changes, or if you want to propose new tutorials,
it might be necessary to understand at least the basics of the <em>git</em>
source versionning system we use.
Alternatively, you may simply write your tutorial in a new text file on
your machine (following <em>Markdown</em> syntax), then simply <a href="https://gitlab.gnome.org/Infrastructure/gimp-web/-/issues/new">open a
report</a>
and upload all the files (the text file as well as images and other
resources) in this report. Do not forget to tell us the license you
chose from <a href="#recommended-licenses">the list given above</a>.</p>
<hr>
<p><small>
A list of legacy tutorials can be found here:
<a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/list-all.html">All (Legacy) Tutorials&nbsp;List</a></p>
<p>Bear in mind that this list is being provided for legacy reasons only.
They were originally made for very old hence outdated versions of <span class="caps">GIMP</span>
and most of them do no use Libre licenses allowing editing.
</small></p>
                </div>
            </div>
        </div>
    </section>

        <div class="row clearfix">
            <div class="column full">
                <h1>Tutorials</h1>
                
            </div>
        </div>
    </div>

    <section class='page_content'>
        <div class='container'>
            <div class='row clearfix'>
                <div class='column full'>
                    <p>🛈 As everything created by the <span class="caps">GIMP</span> project, these tutorials are fully
community-written. Therefore if you find any tutorial incomplete,
or if it contains errors or outdated information, the best thing is to
contribute a fix. Moreover we warmly welcome new tutorials. <a href="#contributing-new-tutorials-or-fixes">See below
for the full contribution
procedure</a>.🛈</p>
<h2 id="beginner">Beginner<a class="headerlink" href="#beginner" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/GIMP_Quickies/"><span class="caps">GIMP</span> Quickies</a><br>
Use <span class="caps">GIMP</span> for simple graphics needs without having to learn advanced image manipulation&nbsp;methods.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Floating_Logo/">Simple Floating Logo</a><br>
This tutorial walks through some basic image and layer manipulation&nbsp;techniques.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/CircleImage/">Making a Circle-Shaped Image</a><br>
How to create a circular-shaped&nbsp;image.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Heart_Shape/">Making a Heart Shape with Selections</a><br>
How to create a heart-shape with&nbsp;selections.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Layer_Masks/">Layer Masks</a><br>
An introduction to using layer masks to modify the opacity of a&nbsp;layer.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Basic_Color_Curves/">Basic Color Curves</a><br>
A first look at the Curves tool and adjusting color tones in an&nbsp;image.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/GIMPProfile/">Your <span class="caps">GIMP</span> Profile (and You)</a><br>
What the <span class="caps">GIMP</span> Profile is and how to use&nbsp;it.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/ImageFormats/">Image Formats Overview</a><br>
Selecting the best image format for your&nbsp;purposes.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Asset_Folders/">Asset Folders</a><br>
Extending <span class="caps">GIMP</span> with new plug-ins, scripts, brushes, and&nbsp;more.</p>
<h2 id="photo-editing">Photo Editing<a class="headerlink" href="#photo-editing" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Digital_Black_and_White_Conversion/">Digital B&amp;W Conversion</a><br>
Detailed conversion tutorial for generating a B&amp;W result from a color&nbsp;image.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Luminosity_Masks/">Luminosity Masks</a><br>
Using multiple layer masks to isolate specific tones in your image for&nbsp;editing.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Tone_Mapping_Using_GIMP_Levels/">Tone Mapping with &#8216;Colors/Exposure&#8217;</a><br>
Using high bit depth <span class="caps">GIMP</span>&#8217;s &#8216;Colors/Exposure&#8217; operation to add exposure compensation to shadows and midtones while retaining highlight&nbsp;details.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Focus_Group/">Focus Group</a><br>
Layer masking and creative filter&nbsp;applications.</p>
<h2 id="painting">Painting<a class="headerlink" href="#painting" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Parametric_Brush/">Parametric Brushes</a><br>
A look at the advantages and flexibility of using Parametric&nbsp;Brushes.</p>
<h2 id="configuration">Configuration<a class="headerlink" href="#configuration" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p><a href="/unix/howtos/tile_cache.html">How to set the tile cache</a><br>
The tile cache tells <span class="caps">GIMP</span> how much memory it can use before swapping some image
data to disk. Setting the size of the tile cache can be critical for the
performance of your&nbsp;system.</p>
<p><a href="/unix/fonts.html">How to install fonts for use with <span class="caps">GIMP</span></a>  </p>
<p><a href="/unix/howtos/gimp-midi.html">How to use <span class="caps">MIDI</span> devices with <span class="caps">GIMP</span></a><br>
<span class="caps">GNU</span>/Linux only&nbsp;procedure.</p>
<h2 id="programming">Programming<a class="headerlink" href="#programming" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Basic_Perl/">Basic <span class="caps">GIMP</span> Perl</a><br>
Learn how to write simple perl scripts using the gimp-perl module (<span class="caps">GNU</span>/Linux users&nbsp;only).</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Automate_Editing_in_GIMP/">Automate Editing</a><br>
Using <span class="caps">GIMP</span> Python to automate a&nbsp;workflow.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/AutomatedJpgToXcf/">Automatic Creation of <span class="caps">XCF</span> from <span class="caps">JPG</span></a><br>
Import <span class="caps">XCF</span> images a directory at a&nbsp;time.</p>
<h2 id="contributing-new-tutorials-or-fixes">Contributing new tutorials or fixes<a class="headerlink" href="#contributing-new-tutorials-or-fixes" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p>You don&#8217;t have to be a developer to participate to the <span class="caps">GIMP</span> project.
Some team members help with design, community management, bug triaging…
and some help with documentation and&nbsp;tutorials!</p>
<p>The only thing we ask of contributors is to use <em>Libre</em> licenses, which
allow anyone to share, redistribute and modify the tutorials. It enables
others to fix tutorials, even years later, even if the original author
is not around anymore. This is the same rules as for our code, making
<span class="caps">GIMP</span> a Free&nbsp;Software.</p>
<p><span id="recommended-licenses"><strong>Recommended licenses</strong></a>&nbsp;are:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://artlibre.org/licence/lal/en/">Free Art&nbsp;1.3</a></li>
<li>Creative Commons <a href="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/">Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0&nbsp;International</a></li>
<li>Creative Commons <a href="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/">Attribution 4.0&nbsp;International</a></li>
<li><a href="https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/"><span class="caps">CC0</span> 1.0 Universal</a>.</li>
</ul>
<p>So you want to contribute? The process is simple, here is an example for
the hypothetical case where you found an error in an existing tutorial.
In such a case of editing existing text, your change will be automatically
considered to be in the same license as chosen by the first&nbsp;author:</p>
<ol>
<li>All tutorial contents can be found on our <a href="https://gitlab.gnome.org/Infrastructure/gimp-web/-/tree/testing/content/tutorials">website&#8217;s
   repository</a>
   (<em>Gitlab</em>). After clicking this link, feel free to browse to understand the file structure: Each
   tutorial is listed in a separate folder and each folder has a file called <code>index.md</code> which
   contains the text of the tutorial. There are many other files that accompany the
   tutorial inside the folder, such as images, screenshots and
   various&nbsp;assets.</li>
<li>Once you found a tutorial, which you want to edit, click the
   <code>index.md</code> link, and you will see a blue button saying &#8220;Edit&#8221;. Click
   it (obviously you need to have created a login first and be&nbsp;connected).</li>
<li><em>Gitlab</em> will propose you to &#8220;fork&#8221; the project because of missing
   permissions.  Press&nbsp;&#8220;fork&#8221;.</li>
<li>Once this is done, make your changes using the
   <a href="https://daringfireball.net/projects/markdown/syntax">Markdown</a>&nbsp;syntax.</li>
<li>When you are happy with your edits, proceed to the bottom of the edit page, notice the &#8220;Commit message&#8221; field.
   Fill in relevant information explaining what you did. Click &#8220;Commit&nbsp;changes&#8221;.</li>
<li>A &#8220;New merge request&#8221; page will appear. Click &#8220;Create merge&nbsp;request&#8221;.</li>
<li>It&#8217;s done! Now all you have to do is wait for one of the core members
   to review and validate your&nbsp;changes.</li>
</ol>
<p>If you just need to change an image (e.g. because it shows an outdated
version of <span class="caps">GIMP</span>), you may select the image in <em>Gitlab</em> and click the
&#8220;Replace&#8221; button. It will propose you to upload a new version and to
write a &#8220;Commit message&#8221; to explain the change. Please write down the
<a href="#recommended-licenses">desired <em>Libre</em> license</a> for the image in the
commit message. Then hit &#8220;Replace&nbsp;file&#8221;.</p>
<p>For more complicated changes, or if you want to propose new tutorials,
it might be necessary to understand at least the basics of the <em>git</em>
source versionning system we use.
Alternatively, you may simply write your tutorial in a new text file on
your machine (following <em>Markdown</em> syntax), then simply <a href="https://gitlab.gnome.org/Infrastructure/gimp-web/-/issues/new">open a
report</a>
and upload all the files (the text file as well as images and other
resources) in this report. Do not forget to tell us the license you
chose from <a href="#recommended-licenses">the list given above</a>.</p>
<hr>
<p><small>
A list of legacy tutorials can be found here:
<a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/list-all.html">All (Legacy) Tutorials&nbsp;List</a></p>
<p>Bear in mind that this list is being provided for legacy reasons only.
They were originally made for very old hence outdated versions of <span class="caps">GIMP</span>
and most of them do no use Libre licenses allowing editing.
</small></p>
                </div>
            </div>
        </div>
    </section>

<h2 id="configuration">Configuration<a class="headerlink" href="#configuration" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>

performance of your&nbsp;system.</p>
<p><a href="/unix/fonts.html">How to install fonts for use with <span class="caps">GIMP</span></a>  </p>
<p><a href="/unix/howtos/gimp-midi.html">How to use <span class="caps">MIDI</span> devices with <span class="caps">GIMP</span></a><br>
<span class="caps">GNU</span>/Linux only&nbsp;procedure.</p>
<h2 id="programming">Programming<a class="headerlink" href="#programming" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Basic_Perl/">Basic <span class="caps">GIMP</span> Perl</a><br>
Learn how to write simple perl scripts using the gimp-perl module (<span class="caps">GNU</span>/Linux users&nbsp;only).</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Automate_Editing_in_GIMP/">Automate Editing</a><br>
Using <span class="caps">GIMP</span> Python to automate a&nbsp;workflow.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/AutomatedJpgToXcf/">Automatic Creation of <span class="caps">XCF</span> from <span class="caps">JPG</span></a><br>
Import <span class="caps">XCF</span> images a directory at a&nbsp;time.</p>
<h2 id="contributing-new-tutorials-or-fixes">Contributing new tutorials or fixes<a class="headerlink" href="#contributing-new-tutorials-or-fixes" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p>You don&#8217;t have to be a developer to participate to the <span class="caps">GIMP</span> project.
Some team members help with design, community management, bug triaging…
and some help with documentation and&nbsp;tutorials!</p>
<p>The only thing we ask of contributors is to use <em>Libre</em> licenses, which
allow anyone to share, redistribute and modify the tutorials. It enables
others to fix tutorials, even years later, even if the original author
is not around anymore. This is the same rules as for our code, making
<span class="caps">GIMP</span> a Free&nbsp;Software.</p>
<p><span id="recommended-licenses"><strong>Recommended licenses</strong></a>&nbsp;are:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://artlibre.org/licence/lal/en/">Free Art&nbsp;1.3</a></li>
<li>Creative Commons <a href="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/">Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0&nbsp;International</a></li>
<li>Creative Commons <a href="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/">Attribution 4.0&nbsp;International</a></li>
<li><a href="https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/"><span class="caps">CC0</span> 1.0 Universal</a>.</li>
</ul>
<p>So you want to contribute? The process is simple, here is an example for
the hypothetical case where you found an error in an existing tutorial.
In such a case of editing existing text, your change will be automatically
considered to be in the same license as chosen by the first&nbsp;author:</p>
<ol>
<li>All tutorial contents can be found on our <a href="https://gitlab.gnome.org/Infrastructure/gimp-web/-/tree/testing/content/tutorials">website&#8217;s
   repository</a>
   (<em>Gitlab</em>). After clicking this link, feel free to browse to understand the file structure: Each
   tutorial is listed in a separate folder and each folder has a file called <code>index.md</code> which
   contains the text of the tutorial. There are many other files that accompany the
   tutorial inside the folder, such as images, screenshots and
   various&nbsp;assets.</li>
<li>Once you found a tutorial, which you want to edit, click the
   <code>index.md</code> link, and you will see a blue button saying &#8220;Edit&#8221;. Click
   it (obviously you need to have created a login first and be&nbsp;connected).</li>
<li><em>Gitlab</em> will propose you to &#8220;fork&#8221; the project because of missing
   permissions.  Press&nbsp;&#8220;fork&#8221;.</li>
<li>Once this is done, make your changes using the
   <a href="https://daringfireball.net/projects/markdown/syntax">Markdown</a>&nbsp;syntax.</li>
<li>When you are happy with your edits, proceed to the bottom of the edit page, notice the &#8220;Commit message&#8221; field.
   Fill in relevant information explaining what you did. Click &#8220;Commit&nbsp;changes&#8221;.</li>
<li>A &#8220;New merge request&#8221; page will appear. Click &#8220;Create merge&nbsp;request&#8221;.</li>
<li>It&#8217;s done! Now all you have to do is wait for one of the core members
   to review and validate your&nbsp;changes.</li>
</ol>
<p>If you just need to change an image (e.g. because it shows an outdated
version of <span class="caps">GIMP</span>), you may select the image in <em>Gitlab</em> and click the
&#8220;Replace&#8221; button. It will propose you to upload a new version and to
write a &#8220;Commit message&#8221; to explain the change. Please write down the
<a href="#recommended-licenses">desired <em>Libre</em> license</a> for the image in the
commit message. Then hit &#8220;Replace&nbsp;file&#8221;.</p>
<p>For more complicated changes, or if you want to propose new tutorials,
it might be necessary to understand at least the basics of the <em>git</em>
source versionning system we use.
Alternatively, you may simply write your tutorial in a new text file on
your machine (following <em>Markdown</em> syntax), then simply <a href="https://gitlab.gnome.org/Infrastructure/gimp-web/-/issues/new">open a
report</a>
and upload all the files (the text file as well as images and other
resources) in this report. Do not forget to tell us the license you
chose from <a href="#recommended-licenses">the list given above</a>.</p>
<hr>
<p><small>
A list of legacy tutorials can be found here:
<a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/list-all.html">All (Legacy) Tutorials&nbsp;List</a></p>
<p>Bear in mind that this list is being provided for legacy reasons only.
They were originally made for very old hence outdated versions of <span class="caps">GIMP</span>
and most of them do no use Libre licenses allowing editing.
</small></p>
                </div>
            </div>
        </div>
    </section>

                <h1>Tutorials</h1>
                
            </div>

    <section class='page_content'>
        <div class='container'>
            <div class='row clearfix'>
                <div class='column full'>
                    <p>🛈 As everything created by the <span class="caps">GIMP</span> project, these tutorials are fully
community-written. Therefore if you find any tutorial incomplete,
or if it contains errors or outdated information, the best thing is to
contribute a fix. Moreover we warmly welcome new tutorials. <a href="#contributing-new-tutorials-or-fixes">See below
for the full contribution
procedure</a>.🛈</p>
<h2 id="beginner">Beginner<a class="headerlink" href="#beginner" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/GIMP_Quickies/"><span class="caps">GIMP</span> Quickies</a><br>
Use <span class="caps">GIMP</span> for simple graphics needs without having to learn advanced image manipulation&nbsp;methods.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Floating_Logo/">Simple Floating Logo</a><br>
This tutorial walks through some basic image and layer manipulation&nbsp;techniques.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/CircleImage/">Making a Circle-Shaped Image</a><br>
How to create a circular-shaped&nbsp;image.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Heart_Shape/">Making a Heart Shape with Selections</a><br>
How to create a heart-shape with&nbsp;selections.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Layer_Masks/">Layer Masks</a><br>
An introduction to using layer masks to modify the opacity of a&nbsp;layer.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Basic_Color_Curves/">Basic Color Curves</a><br>
A first look at the Curves tool and adjusting color tones in an&nbsp;image.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/GIMPProfile/">Your <span class="caps">GIMP</span> Profile (and You)</a><br>
What the <span class="caps">GIMP</span> Profile is and how to use&nbsp;it.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/ImageFormats/">Image Formats Overview</a><br>
Selecting the best image format for your&nbsp;purposes.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Asset_Folders/">Asset Folders</a><br>
Extending <span class="caps">GIMP</span> with new plug-ins, scripts, brushes, and&nbsp;more.</p>
<h2 id="photo-editing">Photo Editing<a class="headerlink" href="#photo-editing" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Digital_Black_and_White_Conversion/">Digital B&amp;W Conversion</a><br>
Detailed conversion tutorial for generating a B&amp;W result from a color&nbsp;image.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Luminosity_Masks/">Luminosity Masks</a><br>
Using multiple layer masks to isolate specific tones in your image for&nbsp;editing.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Tone_Mapping_Using_GIMP_Levels/">Tone Mapping with &#8216;Colors/Exposure&#8217;</a><br>
Using high bit depth <span class="caps">GIMP</span>&#8217;s &#8216;Colors/Exposure&#8217; operation to add exposure compensation to shadows and midtones while retaining highlight&nbsp;details.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Focus_Group/">Focus Group</a><br>
Layer masking and creative filter&nbsp;applications.</p>
<h2 id="painting">Painting<a class="headerlink" href="#painting" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Parametric_Brush/">Parametric Brushes</a><br>
A look at the advantages and flexibility of using Parametric&nbsp;Brushes.</p>
<h2 id="configuration">Configuration<a class="headerlink" href="#configuration" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p><a href="/unix/howtos/tile_cache.html">How to set the tile cache</a><br>
The tile cache tells <span class="caps">GIMP</span> how much memory it can use before swapping some image
data to disk. Setting the size of the tile cache can be critical for the
performance of your&nbsp;system.</p>
<p><a href="/unix/fonts.html">How to install fonts for use with <span class="caps">GIMP</span></a>  </p>
<p><a href="/unix/howtos/gimp-midi.html">How to use <span class="caps">MIDI</span> devices with <span class="caps">GIMP</span></a><br>
<span class="caps">GNU</span>/Linux only&nbsp;procedure.</p>
<h2 id="programming">Programming<a class="headerlink" href="#programming" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Basic_Perl/">Basic <span class="caps">GIMP</span> Perl</a><br>
Learn how to write simple perl scripts using the gimp-perl module (<span class="caps">GNU</span>/Linux users&nbsp;only).</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/Automate_Editing_in_GIMP/">Automate Editing</a><br>
Using <span class="caps">GIMP</span> Python to automate a&nbsp;workflow.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/AutomatedJpgToXcf/">Automatic Creation of <span class="caps">XCF</span> from <span class="caps">JPG</span></a><br>
Import <span class="caps">XCF</span> images a directory at a&nbsp;time.</p>
<h2 id="contributing-new-tutorials-or-fixes">Contributing new tutorials or fixes<a class="headerlink" href="#contributing-new-tutorials-or-fixes" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p>You don&#8217;t have to be a developer to participate to the <span class="caps">GIMP</span> project.
Some team members help with design, community management, bug triaging…
and some help with documentation and&nbsp;tutorials!</p>
<p>The only thing we ask of contributors is to use <em>Libre</em> licenses, which
allow anyone to share, redistribute and modify the tutorials. It enables
others to fix tutorials, even years later, even if the original author
is not around anymore. This is the same rules as for our code, making
<span class="caps">GIMP</span> a Free&nbsp;Software.</p>
<p><span id="recommended-licenses"><strong>Recommended licenses</strong></a>&nbsp;are:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://artlibre.org/licence/lal/en/">Free Art&nbsp;1.3</a></li>
<li>Creative Commons <a href="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/">Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0&nbsp;International</a></li>
<li>Creative Commons <a href="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/">Attribution 4.0&nbsp;International</a></li>
<li><a href="https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/"><span class="caps">CC0</span> 1.0 Universal</a>.</li>
</ul>
<p>So you want to contribute? The process is simple, here is an example for
the hypothetical case where you found an error in an existing tutorial.
In such a case of editing existing text, your change will be automatically
considered to be in the same license as chosen by the first&nbsp;author:</p>
<ol>
<li>All tutorial contents can be found on our <a href="https://gitlab.gnome.org/Infrastructure/gimp-web/-/tree/testing/content/tutorials">website&#8217;s
   repository</a>
   (<em>Gitlab</em>). After clicking this link, feel free to browse to understand the file structure: Each
   tutorial is listed in a separate folder and each folder has a file called <code>index.md</code> which
   contains the text of the tutorial. There are many other files that accompany the
   tutorial inside the folder, such as images, screenshots and
   various&nbsp;assets.</li>
<li>Once you found a tutorial, which you want to edit, click the
   <code>index.md</code> link, and you will see a blue button saying &#8220;Edit&#8221;. Click
   it (obviously you need to have created a login first and be&nbsp;connected).</li>
<li><em>Gitlab</em> will propose you to &#8220;fork&#8221; the project because of missing
   permissions.  Press&nbsp;&#8220;fork&#8221;.</li>
<li>Once this is done, make your changes using the
   <a href="https://daringfireball.net/projects/markdown/syntax">Markdown</a>&nbsp;syntax.</li>
<li>When you are happy with your edits, proceed to the bottom of the edit page, notice the &#8220;Commit message&#8221; field.
   Fill in relevant information explaining what you did. Click &#8220;Commit&nbsp;changes&#8221;.</li>
<li>A &#8220;New merge request&#8221; page will appear. Click &#8220;Create merge&nbsp;request&#8221;.</li>
<li>It&#8217;s done! Now all you have to do is wait for one of the core members
   to review and validate your&nbsp;changes.</li>
</ol>
<p>If you just need to change an image (e.g. because it shows an outdated
version of <span class="caps">GIMP</span>), you may select the image in <em>Gitlab</em> and click the
&#8220;Replace&#8221; button. It will propose you to upload a new version and to
write a &#8220;Commit message&#8221; to explain the change. Please write down the
<a href="#recommended-licenses">desired <em>Libre</em> license</a> for the image in the
commit message. Then hit &#8220;Replace&nbsp;file&#8221;.</p>
<p>For more complicated changes, or if you want to propose new tutorials,
it might be necessary to understand at least the basics of the <em>git</em>
source versionning system we use.
Alternatively, you may simply write your tutorial in a new text file on
your machine (following <em>Markdown</em> syntax), then simply <a href="https://gitlab.gnome.org/Infrastructure/gimp-web/-/issues/new">open a
report</a>
and upload all the files (the text file as well as images and other
resources) in this report. Do not forget to tell us the license you
chose from <a href="#recommended-licenses">the list given above</a>.</p>
<hr>
<p><small>
A list of legacy tutorials can be found here:
<a href="https://www.gimp.org/tutorials/list-all.html">All (Legacy) Tutorials&nbsp;List</a></p>
<p>Bear in mind that this list is being provided for legacy reasons only.
They were originally made for very old hence outdated versions of <span class="caps">GIMP</span>
and most of them do no use Libre licenses allowing editing.
</small></p>
                </div>
            </div>
        </div>
    </section>
